# PLAN — gemini-4-braincells @ Junction 2026

Audience: AI coding agents working for team members. Humans don't read this file.

Location: `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/` on the team server, deliberately OUTSIDE every git repo. NEVER copy, quote at length, or commit PLAN.md, CHALLENGES.md or DECISIONS.log into any repo (including gemini-4-braincells), issue, PR or public page. Keep it current: if you change a decision, interface, port or owner, edit this file in place and add a line to `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/DECISIONS.log`.

Status: DECIDED 2026-11-13 (Fri evening) by Justinas (organiser). Do not reopen the challenge choice.

**To-do list: `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/WIN-CHECKLIST.md`.** Everything we must or will do to win, with nobody assigned. Pick an open item, mark it in progress, tick it when done, and add new work there.

## 1. Decision

- Main challenge: **"Decode the Noise" by Hostinger** (Agentic AI Track). Full brief in `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/CHALLENGES.md`.
- Tech challenges entered:
  - Committed: **Best Use of Gemini API** (Google DeepMind), **Best Use of Nemotron** (NVIDIA), **Best agentic usecase of Oxylabs Web API**.
  - Optional (only if it is clearly part of the product): **Best Use of Context.dev**.
  - Stretch: **Best Use of Gemma** (Google DeepMind).
  - Committed (set up Fri 13 Nov, see section 11): **Best Use of Entire** (MLH). **Best Use of Codex** (OpenAI), only if someone really builds a part with Codex; decide by Saturday 12:00.
- Not entered: everything else.

## 2. Product

Name: **Shill or Chill** (decided 2026-11-13 22:42 by Justinas; replaces the working name "Noise Radar"). Tagline: "Shill or chill? We check the receipts." Tone: youthful and internet-native (stock-forum, meme-page, reels culture), but never at the cost of the honesty story.
- User-facing verdict labels map 1:1 to `clusters.status` (the DB/API values don't change): `coordinated` → 🚩 **Shill** · `likely_organic` → 😎 **Chill** · `insufficient` → 🤷 **Can't tell (yet)**.
- Wording guard: "shill" appears only in the product name, headings and the verdict label for a cluster. Evidence text describes behaviour ("31 accounts, same link, 94 s") and never calls a specific account or person "a shill": we can prove coordination, not payment or intent. The methodology page says this.
- Supporting copy (optional): "Receipts" for the evidence panel, "Certified organic" for a Chill verdict.
- Infra names stay as they are (repo `gemini-4-braincells`, `/opt/noise-radar`, `~/.config/noise-radar`, the `noise-radar.` subdomain); only user-facing text changes.

A live monitor that detects coordinated amplification (bot or campaign behaviour) on Bluesky, explains each flagged cluster with evidence, and reports its own measured error rates.

Thesis, and what we must not build: the generic "paste a post and an LLM says propaganda" tool. Most teams will build that. We detect **coordination between accounts** from behaviour signals, then use LLMs only to explain and to read media. Hostinger judges "strength and honesty of detection logic, including how you handle false positives" over UI. Every design choice should favour measurable precision, calibrated confidence and explicit abstention.

Hard requirement: deployed and running live on **Hostinger** infrastructure with a **public URL** by the end of the hackathon. If it isn't live on Hostinger, we're disqualified from the main prize.

## 3. Architecture

```
Bluesky Jetstream (public websocket, no key)
        │  posts, reposts, likes, follows (filtered collections)
        ▼
ingest ──▶ Postgres (+pgvector) ◀── eval (labelled datasets → metrics)
        │
        ▼
signals: per-window feature extraction → candidate clusters → score + confidence
        │
        ├──▶ media: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL reads images/video frames, near-duplicate media matching
        ├──▶ sources: Oxylabs /scrape linked pages + /search claim origin; Context.dev domain enrichment (optional)
        ▼
analyst: Gemini writes an evidence-based verdict per cluster, or abstains
        ▼
api (FastAPI) ──▶ web dashboard (public URL on Hostinger)
```

### Components and responsibilities

| Dir | Component | Tech | Does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ingest/` | Jetstream consumer | Python 3.12, `websockets` | Subscribes to Bluesky Jetstream (VERIFY current public endpoint, e.g. `wss://jetstream2.us-east.bsky.network/subscribe?wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.post&wantedCollections=app.bsky.feed.repost&wantedCollections=app.bsky.graph.follow`). Normalises events into `posts`, `reposts`, `follows`. Fetches profile metadata (handle, created_at, follower counts) lazily via the public AppView XRPC (`app.bsky.actor.getProfile`, VERIFY host). Optional language/keyword filter to keep volume sane. Must survive reconnects (store the cursor). |
| `signals/` | Coordination detector | Python, numpy/scikit-learn, `datasketch` (MinHash) or pgvector embeddings | Sliding windows (e.g. 10 min / 1 h). Signals: near-duplicate text across distinct accounts (MinHash/embedding similarity), burst synchrony (many accounts posting the same link or text within seconds), account freshness (created recently), shared-link concentration, repost-ring structure (the same accounts reposting each other), handle and name templating patterns, posting-time regularity. Builds candidate clusters (graph connected components or DBSCAN over account-behaviour vectors). Outputs a score in [0,1] with per-signal contributions. **Abstains** below a minimum evidence threshold. |
| `media/` | Nemotron media reader | NVIDIA API (OpenAI-compatible) | For posts with images or video in candidate clusters: describes and extracts text (OCR) from memes and screenshots; finds the same media or message reused across accounts; flags manipulated-context cues. Results feed `signals` as an extra similarity channel and go into the evidence shown to users. |
| `sources/` | Source checking | Oxylabs Web API (`/search`, `/scrape`); Context.dev (optional) | For a cluster's top shared links or claims: scrape the linked page (Oxylabs `/scrape`), search for the earliest or other sources of the claim (Oxylabs `/search`), and optionally enrich the domain (owner, age, brand) via Context.dev. Every fact shown must carry its source URL. Live calls at runtime (Oxylabs' rules: pre-downloaded data alone doesn't count). |
| `analyst/` | Explanation agent | Gemini API (function calling + JSON output) | Per cluster: given signal contributions, sample posts, media findings and source checks, write a short verdict: `coordinated` / `likely organic` / `insufficient evidence`, with confidence, the 3-5 strongest pieces of evidence, the strongest counter-evidence (why it might be organic), and what would change the verdict. It must not invent evidence: it may only cite items passed in. |
| `eval/` | Honesty and metrics | Python | Runs the detector on labelled data and reports precision, recall, F1, false-positive rate and a calibration curve, on held-out data. Results are served by the API and shown on the dashboard ("How accurate are we?"). Also a hand-labelled sample of ~100 live Bluesky clusters (two labellers, agreement reported). |
| `api/` | Backend | FastAPI | Serves clusters, evidence, metrics, health. Schema in §5. |
| `web/` | Dashboard | Vite + React + TypeScript (or plain HTML if short on time) | Live cluster feed, cluster detail page (accounts, timeline, evidence, analyst verdict, counter-evidence, sources), metrics page, "methodology and limits" page. Mobile-usable. |
| `deploy/` | Hostinger deploy | Docker Compose on a Hostinger VPS, Caddy for HTTPS | One `docker compose up -d` brings up ingest, signals worker, api, web, Postgres. Public URL plus a health check. |

### Model use

- **Gemini** (use the current best Gemini model available on the API for `analyst`, and a Flash-class one for cheap batch steps). Required for the Gemini prize: Gemini is central (it writes every verdict and runs tool calls into `sources`).
- **Nemotron 3.5 Super VL** (`nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl-120b-a12b`; VERIFY the exact id on build.nvidia.com). Base URL `https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1`, OpenAI-compatible. The prize REQUIRES Super VL specifically, in core functionality and visible in the demo, plus a text explanation in the submission form (model, what it does, why it matters, how we improved its outputs). Track prompt and schema iterations and eval numbers for that text. Free tier is about 40 req/min per key: every teammate uses their own key; retries with exponential backoff; cache results by media hash.
- **Gemma** (stretch): a small fine-tuned text classifier as a cheap first-pass filter before the expensive models. Only after everything protected works.

### Data for evaluation (VERIFY availability and licence before relying on any)
- Bot detection: Cresci-2017 / other datasets from the Bot Repository (botometer.osome.iu.edu/bot-repository), TwiBot-22 (may need an access request).
- Propaganda techniques in text: SemEval-2020 Task 11 (PTC corpus), SemEval-2023 Task 3 (multilingual persuasion techniques).
- Coordination on Bluesky: no public labelled set we know of. Inject a **synthetic campaign** (scripted accounts in an offline replay, never posted to the real network) into a recorded Jetstream slice to measure recall, and hand-label live clusters to measure precision.
- Never post to Bluesky or create real accounts for testing. Analysis is read-only.

**Live deploy (2026-11-13):** https://noise-radar.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud on Hostinger VPS `srv2159172.hstgr.cloud` (KVM 2, Ubuntu 24.04, 2 vCPU / 8 GB / 96 GB). Hostinger's Docker Manager preinstalled Traefik (owns :80/:443, Let's Encrypt) and a "Hermes Agent" app; leave both alone. Our Caddy sits behind Traefik (`deploy/docker-compose.hostinger.yml`). Deploy = `deploy/deploy.sh [ref]` from the team server as `dev` (SSH alias `hostinger`, root, key `~/.ssh/hostinger_ed25519`); releases in `/opt/noise-radar/releases/<sha>`, secrets only in `/opt/noise-radar/.env` on the VPS (owners add their API keys there, then redeploy). `/version.txt` = deployed sha. Owner: Justinas.

## 4. Protected scope vs stretch

Protected (must ship, in this order):
1. Jetstream ingest → Postgres, running continuously.
2. Coordination signals + clusters with a score, per-signal contributions and abstention.
3. Gemini analyst verdicts with evidence and counter-evidence.
4. Nemotron Super VL in the pipeline on real media, visible in the cluster view.
5. Oxylabs live `/scrape` + `/search` on cluster links, with URLs shown.
6. Eval page with precision and FP rate on held-out data.
7. Live on Hostinger at a public URL.

Stretch: Context.dev enrichment, Gemma first-pass filter, calibration curve, site-owner webhook/alerts, multilingual (Finnish) support, CRACI CI.

## 5. Shared interfaces (contract; change only with a note here and in DECISIONS.log)

Postgres tables (minimum columns):
- `accounts(did PK, handle, display_name, created_at, followers, follows, first_seen)`
- `posts(uri PK, did FK, text, langs[], created_at, reply_to, embed_kind, embed_urls[], media_hashes[], ingested_at)`
- `reposts(uri PK, did, subject_uri, created_at)`; `follows(uri PK, did, subject_did, created_at)`
- `clusters(id PK, window_start, window_end, score, confidence, status /*coordinated|likely_organic|insufficient*/ , signals JSONB, created_at, updated_at)`
- `cluster_members(cluster_id, did, role)`; `cluster_posts(cluster_id, post_uri)`
- `evidence(id PK, cluster_id, kind /*signal|media|source|analyst*/, summary, detail JSONB, source_url, model, created_at)`
- `eval_runs(id PK, dataset, split, precision, recall, f1, fpr, n, details JSONB, created_at)`
- Added 2026-11-13 by kirill (migration `db/migrations/002_ingest_signals.sql`, applied with `python -m common.migrate`; additive except that the raw tables are recreated while empty):
  - Raw tables `posts`, `reposts`, `likes` (new), `follows` are partitioned BY HOUR on `seen_at` (Jetstream server time, from time_us); PK is `(uri, seen_at)`. `created_at` stays the record's client timestamp. Every raw row has `seen_at` and `deleted_at` (deletes are soft). Retention drops old raw partitions (env `INGEST_RETENTION_HOURS`, `INGEST_LIKES_RETENTION_HOURS`). Anything a cluster references must be copied to `cluster_posts_snapshot` / `evidence` (signals does this).
  - `posts` + `cid, reply_root, quote_uri, mentions[], tags[], text_hash`; `media_hashes[]` = image/video blob CIDs; `embed_urls[]` = external card + link facets, normalised (`signals/textnorm.py`). `reposts`/`likes` + `subject_did`.
  - `likes(uri, did, subject_uri, subject_did, created_at, seen_at, deleted_at)`.
  - `accounts` + `did_created_at, pds_host, handle_changes, status, status_at, posts_count, description_len, has_avatar, profile_fetched_at, plc_fetched_at`.
  - `account_events(id, did, kind account|identity, active, status, handle, seq, time_us, event_time, received_at)`: takedowns etc. from Jetstream, stored from the first minute.
  - `ingest_state(stream PK, cursor_time_us, host, last_event_at, events_per_s, updated_at)`.
  - `campaigns(id, first_seen, last_seen, latest_cluster_id, max_score, status)`; `clusters` + `campaign_id, p_value, families_fired, detector_version, window_kind, size, synthetic`.
  - `cluster_posts_snapshot` (copies of posts referenced by clusters; outlives retention); `schema_migrations`.
- Added 2026-11-13 by kirill (PR #6, `signals/README.md` has the exact JSON): `clusters.signals` JSONB = `{detector_version, score, family_scores{content,timing,network,identity}, families_fired[], p_value, null_model{...}, organic_guard_score, signals[{family,name,score,polarity for|against,summary,evidence_id}], status_rule}`. `evidence(kind='signal')` = one row per signal/guard, upserted by name (ids stable while a cluster updates); `detail` has `post_uris`, `post_urls` (bsky.app), `dids`, `profile_urls` plus signal numbers; `model='detector:<version>'`. One `clusters` row per episode (updated in place while the same accounts keep going; check `updated_at`), `campaign_id` links episodes. Status is decided by the detector's rules, not by the LLM.
- PROPOSAL (kirill -> Temuulen/Justinas, NOT decided): the analyst should explain the detector's status instead of deciding it. Keep `status` in the verdict JSON equal to `clusters.status`, and add `llm_assessment` (`coordinated|likely_organic|insufficient`) + `agrees_with_detector` (bool) + `disagreement_reason`. Disagreements are shown in the UI and counted in eval, so "why coordinated?" is never answered with "the LLM said so".

API (FastAPI, JSON):
- `GET /api/health` → `{ok, ingest_lag_s, last_event_at}`
- `GET /api/clusters?status=&min_score=&limit=` → list of cluster summaries
- `GET /api/clusters/{id}` → cluster + members + posts sample + evidence + analyst verdict
- `GET /api/metrics` → latest `eval_runs` per dataset
- `POST /api/analyze` `{text? , url? , handle?}` → ad-hoc check for judges trying their own input (returns signals if the account/post is in our window, otherwise "insufficient evidence" plus text-level findings, clearly labelled as weaker)

Analyst verdict JSON (stored in `evidence.detail` with `kind='analyst'`):
```json
{"status": "coordinated|likely_organic|insufficient", "confidence": 0.0,
 "evidence": [{"evidence_id": 1, "why": "..."}],
 "counter_evidence": ["..."], "would_change_verdict": ["..."], "model": "gemini-..."}
```

## 6. Team, ownership, ports

| Person (server user) | Owns | Dev ports |
|---|---|---|
| Justinas (`dev`) | Hostinger deploy, `eval/`, submission texts, pitch, final say on scope | 3000-3009, 8000-8009 |
| Kirill (`kirill`) | `ingest/`, `signals/`, DB schema | 3010-3019, 8010-8019 |
| Temuulen (`temuulen`) | `analyst/` (Gemini), `sources/` (Oxylabs, Context.dev), `api/` | 3020-3029, 8020-8029 |
| Valtteri (`valtteri`) | `media/` (Nemotron), `web/` dashboard | 3030-3039, 8030-8039 |

Ownership means "decides and reviews", not "only one who may touch". Coordinate through commits (code) and this file (plan). Run `je status` / `je log` before starting. Use your own port block only.

## 7. Working rules for agents

- Work in your person's worktree: `je wt gemini-4-braincells <task>` (branch `<user>/<task>`). Merge `main` (`origin/main`) in often. To land work: push your branch, open a GitHub PR, and **squash-merge** it (`gh pr merge --squash`), then `git pull` in the main checkout. Never merge or commit to `main` locally, never force-push `main`.
- Shared team keys: `/srv/junction-espoo/secrets/team.env` (group-only, outside git; symlink it as `.env` in your worktree). Secrets only in `.env` (gitignored; `.env.example` lists the names): `NVIDIA_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `OXYLABS_USERNAME`, `OXYLABS_PASSWORD`, `CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `HOSTINGER_*`. Never paste keys into prompts, logs, commits or Entire checkpoints.
- Python: 3.12, `uv` for deps, one `pyproject.toml` at the repo root, `ruff`. Tests with `pytest` for `signals/` and `eval/` at minimum (the detection logic is what's judged).
- Every number shown in the UI must come from code in `eval/` or `signals/`, never hard-coded.
- Log every model call (model id, latency, tokens if returned) for the Nemotron/Gemini submission texts.
- Record decisions in `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/DECISIONS.log` (one line: date time, who, decision, why). It stays outside the repo.
- The repo holds code, its README and code-level docs only. Anything strategic (challenge choice, prize tactics, pitch, team split) stays in `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/`.

## 8. Timeline (verified on hackjunction.app/participate/45, Espoo time: preliminary submission Fri 13 Nov 23:55; submissions open Sat 14 Nov 12:00; FINAL deadline Sun 15 Nov 10:00; review Sun 14:00. Hostinger VPS (KVM 2, 1 month free) + AI Router credits: OBTAINED Fri 22:00, see §12. Gemini credits: forms.gle link on tech-challenge 48. Oxylabs: promo code on tech-challenge 32 page, cancel the plan afterwards.)

- Fri night: repo skeleton (`pyproject`, compose, `.env.example`), DB schema, Jetstream ingest running; Hostinger account and VPS obtained at the Hostinger booth; each person gets API keys (NVIDIA, Gemini, Oxylabs); download eval datasets.
- Sat 12:00: signals v1 producing clusters on live data; Gemini verdicts v1; first eval numbers; Codex/Entire go/no-go.
- Sat evening: Nemotron media channel, Oxylabs sources, dashboard v1, deployed on Hostinger.
- Sun morning: freeze features; hand-label sample; final eval run; 2-min backup video; submission texts (Hostinger, Gemini, Nemotron with model explanation, Oxylabs with endpoints used and why); rehearse with judge-style unseen inputs.

## 9. Demo (3 min)

1. Live feed on the public Hostinger URL: clusters appearing in real time.
2. Open one coordinated cluster: timeline of synchronized posts, shared link, fresh accounts; Nemotron shows the same meme reused across 14 accounts; Oxylabs shows the linked site and the earliest source; Gemini's verdict with counter-evidence.
3. Open a cluster we decided is *likely organic* (e.g. a breaking-news burst) and show why we didn't flag it. This is the false-positive story.
4. Metrics page: precision and FP rate on held-out data, plus how we got them. Limits page.
5. Judge's own input via `/api/analyze`.

## 11. Entire (MLH prize) — how we use it, and the $10 credit

Judged on: use of Sessions, Graph, Brain and Trails; clean history; measurable token efficiency.
Repo is set up (PR #2): checkpoint hooks for Claude Code + Codex, Graph + Brain agent guide, GitHub mirror on Entire (eu-central-1), Brain hosted sync. Repo workflow rules are in the repo's `AGENTS.md`.

**Credit ($10 MLH, Justinas's account) pays ONLY for Entire cloud Agents/Runners.** Sessions, checkpoints, Graph, Brain, search, Trails and `entire review` (runs locally on our own Claude Code/Codex) cost $0.
- No project Agents with push triggers. Don't run `entire trail rerun-review`, `entire runner setup --yes` or cloud `entire dispatch` without asking Justinas (use `entire dispatch --local`).
- Keep the credit for one showcase run on Sun morning: one preset Agent (Security or Slop), model Sonnet 5.5, trigger "Run manually", on the final Trail. Expected cost under $1. Auto top-up stays off.

**Each teammate (biggest lever: sessions from all 4 of us):** install Entire in your seat (repo README), `entire login --device`, plugins graph + brain; Codex users approve hooks via `/hooks`. Then every agent session in a worktree is captured.

**Per feature:** Trail → commits made with the agent running (checkpoint trailer) → `entire review general` (verdict posts to the Trail) → `entire trail ci-pr` → `entire trail ready` (undrafts the PR) → squash-merge with the branch's `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers in the squash body (exact command in the repo's AGENTS.md). Codex can't review here (bwrap sandbox fails), so the review profile is Claude Code only. Record durable decisions with `entire brain remember ... --path <category>` (no agent call, free).

**Token-efficiency evidence (Sun morning, owner: whoever has the Entire seat):** run the same 3 code questions twice in fresh sessions, once with Graph and once told not to use it; commit each, then `entire checkpoint tokens <with> --compare <without>`. Report the measured delta as-is, even if small. Also `entire activity` / `entire recap` screenshots for the submission.

## 10. Risks

- Live Bluesky may have few real campaigns during the weekend → keep a recorded slice with a synthetic campaign for a reliable demo, clearly labelled as synthetic.
- Rate limits (NVIDIA ~40 rpm/key, Gemini, Oxylabs) → caching, batching, per-person keys, and only call models on candidate clusters, never on the whole stream.
- Ethics: we flag behaviour patterns, not people's opinions; show confidence and counter-evidence; no doxxing; read-only.
- Hostinger deploy risk → deploy a hello-world on Friday night, then deploy continuously.

## 12. Hostinger VPS (production)

- Obtained Fri 13 Nov 22:00 through Hostinger's hackathon flow, which comes with the "Hermes Agent" template preinstalled (optional for us). Free for 1 month.
- Host `srv2159172.hstgr.cloud`, IPv4 `[REDACTED_IP]`, IPv6 `[REDACTED_IP]`. Ubuntu 24.04.5, 2 vCPU, 7.8 GB RAM, 96 GB disk (90 GB free), Docker 29 + Compose v5. ufw inactive.
- SSH: `ssh -i ~/.ssh/hostinger_ed25519 -o IdentitiesOnly=yes root@[REDACTED_IP]`, from user `dev` on the team server (key made only for this VPS; the host key is in `dev`'s known_hosts). Other teammates: ask Justinas for access. Don't copy the key.
- Already running (from Hostinger): **Traefik** (`/docker/traefik`, host network, holds :80/:443, Let's Encrypt HTTP challenge, resolver `letsencrypt`, docker provider with exposedbydefault=false). **Hermes Agent** (`/docker/hermes-agent-runi`, at `https://hermes-agent-runi.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud`, also published directly on :32768).
- Wildcard DNS: every `*.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud` already resolves to the VPS, so any subdomain gets HTTPS through Traefik labels.
- Deploy approach (PROPOSED, not yet done): keep Traefik. Our stack runs from `/opt/noise-radar` with an override `deploy/docker-compose.hostinger.yml`: Caddy gets no host ports, plus Traefik labels (`Host(noise.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud)`, entrypoint `websecure`, certresolver `letsencrypt`, port 80) and `PUBLIC_DOMAIN=:80`. Caddy still routes `/api` → api and serves `web/`. Proposed public URL: **https://noise.srv2159172.hstgr.cloud** (not live yet).
- Secrets: the VPS keeps its own `.env` (fresh Postgres password, production API keys). Never commit it.

======
# WIN CHECKLIST — gemini-4-braincells @ Junction 2026

Everything we must do or plan to do to win. Nobody is assigned here on purpose: anyone (person or agent) picks an open item, does it and ticks it.
- Mark done as `[x]` and add the date and time (e.g. `[x] … (Sat 09:40)`). If you're working on an item, add `(in progress: <user>)` so nobody duplicates it, and remove it when you finish.
- This file lives in `/srv/junction-espoo/plan/` like PLAN.md: outside git. Never copy it into a repo, issue, PR or public page. The design and contracts are in PLAN.md, and the official rules are in CHALLENGES.md.

# eval/: how often is the detector right?

Every number the dashboard shows about our own accuracy comes from here, through `eval_runs`
(`GET /api/metrics` serves the latest row per `dataset` + `split`).

```bash
uv run python -m eval copy-slices                                # keep finished recorded hours
uv run python -m eval recall --split dev                          # print the table only
uv run python -m eval recall --split heldout --database-url URL   # ...and write an eval_runs row
uv run pytest tests/test_eval_recall.py                           # offline; no DB, no network
```

`--database-url` is opt-in: without it nothing is written anywhere. Other flags: `--repeats N`
(campaigns per level per window, default 5), `--levels L1 L2`, `--workers 4`, `--json-out FILE`,
`--hours YYYYMMDDHH ...` (ad-hoc hours instead of a split). Ad-hoc or partial runs (`--hours`,
`--max-windows`, a subset of `--levels`) are refused with `--database-url`, so they can't replace
a split's published row.

## Datasets and splits

| `dataset` | What it measures | Columns filled |
|---|---|---|
| `synthetic_campaigns` | **recall**: share of injected synthetic campaigns the detector marks `coordinated` | `recall`, `n`, `details` (`precision`, `f1`, `fpr` stay NULL: no negatives here) |

`split` is `dev` (we may look at it while changing the detector or the eval) or `heldout`
(reported only; never tune thresholds, hit rules or synth settings on it). **Split rule** (shared
by every eval here): a window belongs to the UTC hour it starts in; **odd hours are `heldout`,
even hours are `dev`** (`eval/slices.py`, `split_of_hour`). Whole hours, so one burst never
straddles both. `--split` uses every recorded hour of that parity found under `--slice`; the hours
and windows actually used are stored in `details`.

19:50 window is complete), 20 (`dev`), 21 (`heldout`). Disclosure: the 19:50 window was used for
a one-window smoke test before the split rule was fixed; nothing was tuned on it.

The recorder keeps raw hours for 24 h only, so these hours are copied (same layout) to
`/srv/junction-espoo/data/eval-slices/jetstream/` on the team server (shared, outside git).

## How the recall eval works (`recall.py`)

1. **Windows** (`slices.py`): the recording is cut into clock-aligned 10-minute windows (the live
   worker's main window). Each window is built in memory with the ingest normaliser and the same
   rules as `signals.window.load_window`: posts in the window; likes/reposts/follows whose subject
   got 2..`max_key_accounts` distinct accounts; per-second background counts of every event; events
   duplicated across Jetstream hosts kept once. No database is involved. Windows the recording
   doesn't fully cover (start, end, or a hole over 60 s) are skipped and listed in `details`.
2. **Inject**: for each window, level (L1, L2, L3) and repeat, one campaign from
   `signals.synth.campaign` (12 accounts, `did:plc:synth*`, seeded per window/level/repeat) is
   added to the real window with `signals.synth.inject`. One campaign per detector run, so
   campaigns never help each other. Nothing is posted anywhere and nothing touches a database.
3. **Detect**: `signals.detect.detect`, the live worker's entry point and config. Only synthetic
   accounts get account info (age, followers...); real accounts in an offline window have none.
4. **Score**: a campaign is **caught** when >= 50% of its accounts are in clusters with status
   `coordinated`. **Surfaced** (reported, not counted as caught) = >= 50% in clusters the worker
   would store at any status, i.e. visible on the dashboard as "can't tell" or "chill". Recall =
   caught / injected, with a 95% Wilson interval, overall and per level.

Levels (from `signals/synth.py`): **L1** copy-paste text + link, brand-new templated accounts,
< 1 min burst. **L2** light paraphrase, 3-8 week old accounts, ~5 min jitter. **L3** heavy
paraphrase, aged accounts with followers, slow drip over the whole window.

`details` holds: `per_level` (caught, surfaced, CI, best-cluster status counts),
`detector_version`, `eval_commit`, `hit_rule`, the windows used and skipped, the baseline
cluster counts of each window without injection, and every trial.

## Limits and findings (honest list)

- These are **synthetic** campaigns written by us, so recall here is an upper bound for campaigns
  that look like our generator, not a measured recall on real-world operations.
- One campaign shape per level (12 accounts, one link, four promoted posts). Larger, smaller or

depends on it. Step 2 holds for small edits, follow-up work, and tasks that already

from api.schemas import (
    ClusterDetail,

_SUMMARY_COLS = """
    c.id, c.status, c.score, c.confidence, c.p_value, c.size, c.families_fired, c.window_kind,
    c.window_start, c.window_end, c.campaign_id, c.synthetic, c.updated_at, c.signals,
    v.detail AS verdict_detail, v.created_at AS verdict_at
"""
_LATEST_VERDICT = """
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT detail, created_at FROM evidence
        WHERE cluster_id = c.id AND kind = 'analyst'
        ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 1
    ) v ON true
"""


def bsky_post_url(uri: str) -> str | None:
    """at://did/app.bsky.feed.post/rkey -> https://bsky.app/profile/did/post/rkey"""
    parts = uri.removeprefix("at://").split("/") if uri.startswith("at://") else []
    if len(parts) == 3 and parts[1] == "app.bsky.feed.post":
        return f"https://bsky.app/profile/{parts[0]}/post/{parts[2]}"
    return None


def _summary(row: dict, *, n_signals: int = 3) -> ClusterSummary:
    signals = (row.get("signals") or {}).get("signals") or []
    v = row.get("verdict_detail")
    return ClusterSummary(
        **{k: row[k] for k in ClusterSummary.model_fields if k in row and k != "verdict"},
        top_signals=[SignalBrief(**s) for s in signals if s.get("polarity") == "for"][:n_signals],
        verdict=(
            VerdictBrief(
                status=v["status"],
                confidence=v.get("confidence", 0.0),
                summary=v.get("summary"),
                model=v.get("model"),
                created_at=row["verdict_at"],
            )
            if v
            else None
        ),
    )


def _like(text: str) -> str:
    return "%" + text.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("%", "\\%").replace("_", "\\_") + "%"


class Store:
    def __init__(self, conn: psycopg.Connection):
        self.conn = conn

    def list_clusters(
        self,
        *,
        status: str | None,
        min_score: float,
        limit: int,
        include_synthetic: bool,
    ) -> list[ClusterSummary]:
        rows = self.conn.execute(
            f"""
            SELECT {_SUMMARY_COLS} FROM clusters c {_LATEST_VERDICT}
            WHERE c.score >= %(min_score)s
              AND (%(status)s::text IS NULL OR c.status = %(status)s)

            ORDER BY c.window_end DESC, c.id DESC
            LIMIT %(limit)s
            """,

                "min_score": min_score,
                "status": status,
                "synthetic": include_synthetic,
                "limit": limit,

        ).fetchall()

            WHERE m.cluster_id = %s
            ORDER BY (m.role = 'core') DESC, m.did
            LIMIT %s
            """,

        posts = self.conn.execute(

# Production stack for the Hostinger VPS. From the repo root:
#   docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml --env-file .env up -d --build
name: noise-radar

services:
  db:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg16
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${POSTGRES_USER}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${POSTGRES_DB}
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
      - ../db/schema.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/001-schema.sql:ro
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U $${POSTGRES_USER} -d $${POSTGRES_DB}"]
      interval: 5s
      retries: 10

  api:
    build: { context: .., dockerfile: Dockerfile }
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: ../.env
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://${POSTGRES_USER}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
    depends_on:
      db: { condition: service_healthy }
      migrate: { condition: service_completed_successfully }

  # Applies db/schema.sql + db/migrations/*.sql (idempotent), then exits.
  migrate:
    build: { context: .., dockerfile: Dockerfile }
    command: ["python", "-m", "common.migrate"]
    env_file: ../.env
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://${POSTGRES_USER}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}@db:5432/${POSTGRES_DB}
    depends_on: { db: { condition: service_healthy } }
    restart: "no"

# Override for the Hostinger VPS. Its Docker Manager already runs Traefik on :80/:443
# (host network, Let's Encrypt, /docker/traefik). Caddy stays our in-stack router but takes
# no host ports; Traefik sends https://$PUBLIC_HOST to it and handles the certificate.
# HTTP->HTTPS is redirected globally by that Traefik. `ports: !reset` needs Compose >= 2.24.4.
#   docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker-compose.hostinger.yml --env-file .env up -d --build
services:
  caddy:
    ports: !reset []
    environment:
      PUBLIC_DOMAIN: ":80"
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.routers.noise-radar.rule=Host(`${PUBLIC_HOST:?set PUBLIC_HOST in .env}`)
      - traefik.http.routers.noise-radar.entrypoints=websecure
      - traefik.http.routers.noise-radar.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt
      - traefik.http.services.noise-radar.loadbalancer.server.port=80

"""Hand labels on live clusters -> live precision, false-positive rate and labeller agreement.

    python -m eval labels sample --name live-v1 --n 100   # freeze a stratified sample (reads the DB)
    python -m eval labels serve --port 8000               # labelling page (eval/label_server.py)
    python -m eval labels score --name live-v1            # print; + --database-url URL to write

Files live outside git under LABELS_DIR (default /srv/junction-espoo/data/labels): the sample is
real Bluesky content, so it isn't committed. `samples/<name>.json` is the frozen sample (write-once),
`<name>.labels.jsonl` is append-only (latest record per labeller and item wins).

Blinding: each sample item has a `detector` block (status, score...) and an `evidence` block (what
the labeller sees). The labelling server only ever sends `evidence`, and items are numbered in a
shuffled order, so neither the status, the score nor the cluster id reaches the labeller.
"""

import argparse
import fcntl
import json
import logging
import math
import os
import random
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path

log = logging.getLogger("eval.labels")

DATASET = "live_hand_labels"
LABELS = ("coordinated", "organic", "cant_tell")
DEFINITE = ("coordinated", "organic")
STATUSES = ("coordinated", "likely_organic", "insufficient")
# Share of the sample each detector status gets before capping at what exists. Coordinated is
# oversampled (it is rare and its precision is the headline); weights undo this for FPR.
STATUS_SHARE = {"coordinated": 0.4, "likely_organic": 0.3, "insufficient": 0.3}
SAMPLE_RULE_VERSION = "labels-sample-v1"


def labels_dir() -> Path:
    return Path(os.environ.get("LABELS_DIR", "/srv/junction-espoo/data/labels"))


def sample_path(name: str, root: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    return (root or labels_dir()) / "samples" / f"{name}.json"


def labels_path(name: str, root: Path | None = None) -> Path:
    return (root or labels_dir()) / f"{name}.labels.jsonl"


def split_of(ts: datetime) -> str:
    """Shared split rule (eval/slices.py): odd UTC hours are heldout, even hours dev."""
    return "heldout" if ts.astimezone(UTC).hour % 2 else "dev"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sampling (pure part)


@dataclass
class Candidate:
    cluster_id: int
    campaign_id: int | None
    status: str
    score: float
    window_start: datetime


def one_per_campaign(cands: list[Candidate], rng: random.Random) -> list[Candidate]:
    """Episodes of one campaign (and the 10 min / 1 h windows over the same accounts) are near
    copies; labelling several would count one judgement many times. Keep one random episode."""
    groups: dict[object, list[Candidate]] = defaultdict(list)
    for c in sorted(cands, key=lambda c: c.cluster_id):
        groups[c.campaign_id if c.campaign_id is not None else ("solo", c.cluster_id)].append(c)
    return sorted((rng.choice(g) for g in groups.values()), key=lambda c: c.cluster_id)


def _largest_remainder(total: int, weights: dict, caps: dict) -> dict:
    """Split `total` over keys in proportion to `weights`, never above `caps`; what a capped key
    can't take goes to the others (same proportions)."""
    alloc = {k: 0 for k in weights}
    left = min(total, sum(caps.values()))
    while left > 0:
        open_ = {k: w for k, w in weights.items() if alloc[k] < caps[k] and w > 0}
        if not open_:
            break
        wsum = sum(open_.values())
        raw = {k: left * w / wsum for k, w in open_.items()}
        give = {k: min(int(math.floor(v)), caps[k] - alloc[k]) for k, v in raw.items()}
        rest = left - sum(give.values())
        for k in sorted(open_, key=lambda k: (-(raw[k] - math.floor(raw[k])), str(k))):
            if rest <= 0:
                break
            if alloc[k] + give[k] < caps[k]:
                give[k] += 1
                rest -= 1
        if sum(give.values()) == 0:
            break
        for k, v in give.items():
            alloc[k] += v
        left -= sum(give.values())
    return alloc


def score_bands(cands: list[Candidate], n_bands: int, rng: random.Random) -> list[list[Candidate]]:
    """Equal-count bands by score rank (ties broken at random), lowest score first."""
    keyed = sorted(cands, key=lambda c: (c.score, rng.random()))
    n_bands = max(1, min(n_bands, len(keyed)))
    return [keyed[len(keyed) * b // n_bands : len(keyed) * (b + 1) // n_bands] for b in range(n_bands)]


def stratified_sample(
    cands: list[Candidate], n: int, seed: int, n_bands: int = 4
) -> tuple[list[dict], dict]:
    """Stratify by detector status x score band. Returns (picked, strata) where each picked entry
    is {candidate, stratum, weight} and weight = stratum population / stratum sample size."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    by_status = {s: [c for c in cands if c.status == s] for s in STATUSES}
    quota = _largest_remainder(
        n, STATUS_SHARE, {s: len(v) for s, v in by_status.items()}
    )
    picked, strata = [], {}
    for status in STATUSES:
        bands = score_bands(by_status[status], n_bands, rng) if by_status[status] else []
        band_quota = _largest_remainder(
            quota[status], {b: 1 for b in range(len(bands))}, {b: len(x) for b, x in enumerate(bands)}
        )
        for b, members in enumerate(bands):
            k = band_quota[b]
            key = f"{status}/b{b}"
            strata[key] = {
                "status": status,
                "band": b,
                "score_min": round(min(c.score for c in members), 4),
                "score_max": round(max(c.score for c in members), 4),
                "population": len(members),
                "sampled": k,
            }
            for c in rng.sample(members, k):
                picked.append({"candidate": c, "stratum": key, "weight": len(members) / k})
    rng.shuffle(picked)  # labelling order mixes strata
    return picked, strata


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- evidence (pure part)


def bsky_post_url(uri: str | None) -> str | None:
    parts = uri.removeprefix("at://").split("/") if uri and uri.startswith("at://") else []
    if len(parts) == 3 and parts[1] == "app.bsky.feed.post":
        return f"https://bsky.app/profile/{parts[0]}/post/{parts[2]}"
    return None


def _iso(t: datetime | None) -> str | None:
    return t.astimezone(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds") if t else None


def _age_days(created: datetime | None, at: datetime) -> float | None:
    return round((at - created).total_seconds() / 86400, 1) if created else None


def build_evidence(
    window_start: datetime,
    window_end: datetime,
    window_kind: str | None,
    members: list[dict],
    posts: list[dict],
    actions: list[dict],
    subject_texts: dict[str, dict],
    extra: list[dict],
    *,
    n_buckets: int = 30,
    max_posts: int = 30,
    max_members: int = 80,
) -> dict:
    """What a labeller sees: raw behaviour of the cluster's accounts in its window. Nothing here
    comes from the detector's output (no status, score, p-value, signal or analyst text).

    members: {did, role, handle, display_name, created_at, did_created_at, followers, follows,
              posts_count, has_avatar, description_len, status}
    posts:   {uri, did, text, created_at, seen_at, reply_to, quote_uri, embed_urls, media_hashes,
              text_hash}
    actions: {kind like|repost|follow, did, subject_uri, subject_did, seen_at}
    extra:   media/source evidence rows {kind, summary, source_url}
    """
    handle = {m["did"]: m.get("handle") or m["did"] for m in members}
    member_dids = set(handle)
    span = max((window_end - window_start).total_seconds(), 1.0)

    # timeline: every member action in the window, by kind
    tl = {k: [0] * n_buckets for k in ("post", "like", "repost", "follow")}
    events = [("post", p["seen_at"]) for p in posts] + [(a["kind"], a["seen_at"]) for a in actions]
    for kind, t in events:
        if t is None:
            continue
        b = int((t - window_start).total_seconds() / span * n_buckets)
        tl[kind][min(max(b, 0), n_buckets - 1)] += 1

    # per-member activity
    act = defaultdict(Counter)
    for p in posts:
        act[p["did"]]["post"] += 1
    for a in actions:
        act[a["did"]][a["kind"]] += 1

    # things several members engaged with (likes, reposts, replies, quotes)
    eng: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for a in actions:
        if a["kind"] in ("like", "repost") and a.get("subject_uri"):
            e = eng.setdefault(a["subject_uri"], {"kinds": Counter(), "dids": set(), "times": []})
            e["kinds"][a["kind"]] += 1
            e["dids"].add(a["did"])
            e["times"].append(a["seen_at"])
    for p in posts:
        for kind, uri in (("reply", p.get("reply_to")), ("quote", p.get("quote_uri"))):
            if uri:
                e = eng.setdefault(uri, {"kinds": Counter(), "dids": set(), "times": []})
                e["kinds"][kind] += 1
                e["dids"].add(p["did"])
                e["times"].append(p["seen_at"])
    targets = []
    for uri, e in eng.items():
        if len(e["dids"]) < 2:
            continue
        ts = sorted(t for t in e["times"] if t)
        subj = subject_texts.get(uri) or {}
        author = uri.removeprefix("at://").split("/")[0] if uri.startswith("at://") else None
        targets.append(
            {
                "url": bsky_post_url(uri),
                "uri": uri,
                "accounts": len(e["dids"]),
                "actions": dict(e["kinds"]),
                "spread_s": round((ts[-1] - ts[0]).total_seconds()) if len(ts) > 1 else 0,
                "author_is_member": author in member_dids,
                "text": (subj.get("text") or "")[:280] or None,
            }
        )
    targets.sort(key=lambda t: (-t["accounts"], -sum(t["actions"].values()), t["uri"]))

    follow_targets = Counter()
    follow_dids = defaultdict(set)
    for a in actions:
        if a["kind"] == "follow" and a.get("subject_did"):
            follow_dids[a["subject_did"]].add(a["did"])
    for d, s in follow_dids.items():
        if len(s) >= 2:
            follow_targets[d] = len(s)

    links = defaultdict(lambda: {"posts": 0, "dids": set()})
    for p in posts:
        for u in p.get("embed_urls") or []:
            links[u]["posts"] += 1
            links[u]["dids"].add(p["did"])
    shared_links = sorted(
        (
            {"url": u, "posts": v["posts"], "accounts": len(v["dids"])}
            for u, v in links.items()
        ),
        key=lambda x: (-x["accounts"], -x["posts"], x["url"]),
    )

    texts = defaultdict(lambda: {"posts": 0, "dids": set(), "text": None})
    for p in posts:
        key = p.get("text_hash") or ((p.get("text") or "").strip().lower() or None)
        if key:
            texts[key]["posts"] += 1
            texts[key]["dids"].add(p["did"])
            texts[key]["text"] = texts[key]["text"] or p.get("text")
    repeated = sorted(
        (
            {"text": (v["text"] or "")[:280], "posts": v["posts"], "accounts": len(v["dids"])}
            for v in texts.values()
            if v["posts"] >= 2
        ),
        key=lambda x: (-x["accounts"], -x["posts"]),
    )

    ps = sorted(posts, key=lambda p: (p["seen_at"] or window_start, p["uri"]))
    if len(ps) > max_posts:  # evenly spaced over the window, so a long tail isn't cut off
        ps = [ps[i * len(ps) // max_posts] for i in range(max_posts)]
    post_rows = [
        {
            "url": bsky_post_url(p["uri"]),
            "handle": handle.get(p["did"], p["did"]),
            "text": (p.get("text") or "")[:500],
            "seen_at": _iso(p["seen_at"]),
            "t_s": round((p["seen_at"] - window_start).total_seconds()) if p["seen_at"] else None,
            "reply": bool(p.get("reply_to")),
            "quote": bool(p.get("quote_uri")),
            "links": list(p.get("embed_urls") or [])[:3],
            "media": len(p.get("media_hashes") or []),
        }
        for p in ps
    ]

    member_rows = []

    member_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["role"] != "core", -sum(r["activity"].values()), r["handle"]))
    ages = [r["age_days"] for r in member_rows if r["age_days"] is not None]

def fetch_candidates(conn, settled_min: float, include_synthetic: bool = False) -> list[Candidate]:
    rows = conn.execute(
        """
        SELECT id, campaign_id, status, score, window_start FROM clusters
        WHERE updated_at < now() - make_interval(secs => %s)
          AND (%s OR NOT coalesce(synthetic, false))
        ORDER BY id
        """,
        (settled_min * 60, include_synthetic),
    ).fetchall()
    return [Candidate(r[0], r[1], r[2], float(r[3]), r[4]) for r in rows]


def fetch_cluster(conn, cluster_id: int) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    """(detector block, evidence block) for one cluster, read from the live tables."""
    c = conn.execute(
        """
        SELECT id, campaign_id, status, score, confidence, p_value, families_fired, size,
               window_kind, detector_version, window_start, window_end, updated_at
        FROM clusters WHERE id = %s
        """,
        (cluster_id,),
    ).fetchone()
    cols = ["cluster_id", "campaign_id", "status", "score", "confidence", "p_value",
            "families_fired", "size", "window_kind", "detector_version", "window_start",
            "window_end", "updated_at"]  # fmt: skip
    det = dict(zip(cols, c, strict=True))
    ws, we = det["window_start"], det["window_end"]
    mcols = ["did", "role", "handle", "display_name", "created_at", "did_created_at",
             "followers", "follows", "posts_count", "has_avatar", "description_len", "status"]  # fmt: skip
    members = [
        dict(zip(mcols, r, strict=True))
        for r in conn.execute(
            f"""
            SELECT m.did, m.role, {", ".join("a." + x for x in mcols[2:])}
            FROM cluster_members m LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.did = m.did
            WHERE m.cluster_id = %s
            """,
            (cluster_id,),
        ).fetchall()
    ]
    dids = [m["did"] for m in members]
    pcols = ["uri", "did", "text", "created_at", "seen_at", "reply_to", "quote_uri",
             "embed_urls", "media_hashes", "text_hash"]  # fmt: skip
    sel = ", ".join(pcols)
    posts = {
        r[0]: dict(zip(pcols, r, strict=True))
        for r in conn.execute(
            f"""
            SELECT DISTINCT ON (uri) {sel} FROM posts
            WHERE did = ANY(%s) AND seen_at >= %s AND seen_at <= %s AND deleted_at IS NULL
            ORDER BY uri, seen_at
            """,
            (dids, ws, we),
        ).fetchall()
    }
    for r in conn.execute(  # snapshots outlive raw-table retention
        f"""
        SELECT {", ".join("s." + x for x in pcols)} FROM cluster_posts cp
        JOIN cluster_posts_snapshot s ON s.uri = cp.post_uri
        WHERE cp.cluster_id = %s AND s.deleted_at IS NULL
        """,
        (cluster_id,),
    ).fetchall():
        posts.setdefault(r[0], dict(zip(pcols, r, strict=True)))
    actions = [
        {"kind": r[0], "did": r[1], "subject_uri": r[2], "subject_did": r[3], "seen_at": r[4]}
        for r in conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT 'like', did, subject_uri, subject_did, seen_at FROM likes
             WHERE did = ANY(%(d)s) AND seen_at >= %(s)s AND seen_at <= %(e)s AND deleted_at IS NULL
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 'repost', did, subject_uri, subject_did, seen_at FROM reposts
             WHERE did = ANY(%(d)s) AND seen_at >= %(s)s AND seen_at <= %(e)s AND deleted_at IS NULL
            UNION ALL
            SELECT 'follow', did, NULL, subject_did, seen_at FROM follows
             WHERE did = ANY(%(d)s) AND seen_at >= %(s)s AND seen_at <= %(e)s AND deleted_at IS NULL
            """,
            {"d": dids, "s": ws, "e": we},
        ).fetchall()
    ]
    subj = Counter(a["subject_uri"] for a in actions if a["subject_uri"])
    subj.update(p["reply_to"] for p in posts.values() if p["reply_to"])
    subj.update(p["quote_uri"] for p in posts.values() if p["quote_uri"])
    top = [u for u, _ in subj.most_common(40)]
    subject_texts = {}
    if top:
        for r in conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT DISTINCT ON (uri) uri, did, text FROM posts WHERE uri = ANY(%s)
            UNION ALL
            SELECT uri, did, text FROM cluster_posts_snapshot WHERE uri = ANY(%s)
            """,
            (top, top),
        ).fetchall():
            subject_texts.setdefault(r[0], {"did": r[1], "text": r[2]})
    extra = [
        {"kind": r[0], "summary": r[1], "source_url": r[2]}
        for r in conn.execute(
            """
            SELECT kind, summary, source_url FROM evidence
            WHERE cluster_id = %s AND kind IN ('media', 'source') ORDER BY kind, id
            """,
            (cluster_id,),
        ).fetchall()
    ]
    ev = build_evidence(
        ws, we, det["window_kind"], members, list(posts.values()), actions, subject_texts, extra
    )
    det = {
        **det,
        "score": round(float(det["score"]), 4),
        "confidence": None if det["confidence"] is None else round(float(det["confidence"]), 4),
        "p_value": None if det["p_value"] is None else float(det["p_value"]),
        "window_start": _iso(ws),
        "window_end": _iso(we),
        "updated_at": _iso(det["updated_at"]),
    }
    return det, ev


def _git_sha() -> str | None:
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(Path(__file__).parent), "describe", "--always", "--dirty"],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=5,
        )
        return out.stdout.strip() or None
    except Exception:
        return None


def build_sample(conn, name: str, n: int, seed: int, settled_min: float, source: str) -> dict:
    cands = fetch_candidates(conn, settled_min)
    reps = one_per_campaign(cands, random.Random(seed))
    picked, strata = stratified_sample(reps, n, seed)
    items = []
    for k, p in enumerate(picked, 1):
        det, ev = fetch_cluster(conn, p["candidate"].cluster_id)
        items.append(
            {
                "item": k,
                "stratum": p["stratum"],
                "weight": round(p["weight"], 6),
                "split": split_of(p["candidate"].window_start),
                "detector": det,
                "evidence": ev,
            }
        )
        if k % 10 == 0:
            log.info("%d/%d clusters snapshotted", k, len(picked))
    return {
        "name": name,
        "rule_version": SAMPLE_RULE_VERSION,
        "created_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "source": source,
        "seed": seed,
        "eval_commit": _git_sha(),
        "rule": (
            f"clusters not updated for >= {settled_min:g} min, synthetic excluded; one random "
            "episode per campaign; stratified by detector status (target shares "
            f"{STATUS_SHARE}) x 4 equal-count score bands; weight = stratum population / sampled"
        ),
        "population": {
            "clusters": len(cands),
            "campaigns": len(reps),
            "by_status": dict(Counter(c.status for c in reps)),
        },
        "strata": strata,
        "detector_versions": dict(Counter(i["detector"]["detector_version"] for i in items)),
        "items": items,
    }

def append_record(path: Path, rec: dict) -> dict:
    """Append one label/adjudication record (JSONL, flock'd, fsync'd)."""
    if rec.get("label") not in LABELS:
        raise ValueError(f"label must be one of {LABELS}")
    rec = {"at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"), **rec}
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
        f.write(json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())
        fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
    return rec


def load_records(path: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, dict[int, dict]], dict[int, dict]]:
    """-> (labels[labeller][item] = latest record, adjudications[item] = latest record)."""
    labels: dict[str, dict[int, dict]] = defaultdict(dict)
    adj: dict[int, dict] = {}
    if not path.exists():
        return {}, {}
    for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        r = json.loads(line)
        if r.get("type") == "adjudication":
            adj[int(r["item"])] = r
        else:
            labels[r["labeller"]][int(r["item"])] = r
    return dict(labels), adj


def clean_name(name: str) -> str:
    s = "".join(ch for ch in name.strip().lower() if ch.isalnum() or ch in "-_.")
    if not s or len(s) > 32:
        raise ValueError("labeller name: 1-32 letters, digits, - _ .")
    return s


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- scoring


def wilson(k: float, n: float, z: float = 1.96) -> tuple[float, float] | None:
    """95% Wilson score interval; k and n may be fractional (effective counts)."""
    if n <= 0:
        return None
    p = k / n
    d = 1 + z * z / n
    c = (p + z * z / (2 * n)) / d
    h = z * math.sqrt(max(p * (1 - p) / n + z * z / (4 * n * n), 0.0)) / d
    return round(max(0.0, c - h), 4), round(min(1.0, c + h), 4)


def weighted_rate(hits: list[tuple[bool, float]]) -> dict:
    """Rate of True among (hit, weight) pairs, weighted, with a Wilson interval on the Kish
    effective sample size n_eff = (sum w)^2 / sum w^2. Equal weights give the plain k/n."""
    n = len(hits)
    k = sum(h for h, _ in hits)
    if n == 0:
        return {"k": 0, "n": 0, "rate": None, "ci95": None, "n_eff": 0}
    sw = sum(w for _, w in hits)
    rate = sum(w for h, w in hits if h) / sw
    n_eff = sw * sw / sum(w * w for _, w in hits)
    return {
        "k": k,
        "n": n,
        "rate": round(rate, 4),
        "ci95": wilson(rate * n_eff, n_eff),
        "n_eff": round(n_eff, 1),
    }


def cohen_kappa(pairs: list[tuple[str, str]], categories: tuple[str, ...] = LABELS) -> dict:
    """Cohen's kappa for two raters, with the large-sample approximate SE
    sqrt(po(1-po) / (n (1-pe)^2)) and a 95% interval clipped to [-1, 1]."""
    n = len(pairs)
    if n == 0:
        return {"kappa": None, "n": 0, "observed": None, "expected": None, "ci95": None}
    po = sum(a == b for a, b in pairs) / n
    ca, cb = Counter(a for a, _ in pairs), Counter(b for _, b in pairs)
    pe = sum(ca[c] * cb[c] for c in categories) / (n * n)
    if pe >= 1.0:  # both raters used one category for everything: kappa undefined
        return {"kappa": None, "n": n, "observed": round(po, 4), "expected": 1.0, "ci95": None}
    kappa = (po - pe) / (1 - pe)
    se = math.sqrt(po * (1 - po) / (n * (1 - pe) ** 2))
    return {
        "kappa": round(kappa, 4),
        "n": n,
        "observed": round(po, 4),
        "expected": round(pe, 4),
        "ci95": (round(max(-1.0, kappa - 1.96 * se), 4), round(min(1.0, kappa + 1.96 * se), 4)),
    }


def pick_pair(labels: dict[str, dict[int, dict]]) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    """The two labellers who labelled the most items in common (ties: by name)."""
    names = sorted(labels)
    best = None
    for i, a in enumerate(names):
        for b in names[i + 1 :]:
            common = len(labels[a].keys() & labels[b].keys())
            if best is None or common > best[0]:
                best = (common, a, b)
    return (best[1], best[2]) if best else None


def final_labels(
    items: list[int], labels: dict[str, dict[int, dict]], adj: dict[int, dict]
) -> dict[int, dict]:
    """item -> {label|None, how}. An adjudication wins; else all labellers agree (>= 2 of them);
    else unresolved ('single' = one labeller so far, 'disagree' = needs adjudication)."""
    out = {}
    for it in items:
        if it in adj:
            out[it] = {"label": adj[it]["label"], "how": "adjudicated"}
            continue
        given = [labels[name][it]["label"] for name in labels if it in labels[name]]
        if len(given) >= 2 and len(set(given)) == 1:
            out[it] = {"label": given[0], "how": "agreed"}
        elif len(given) >= 2:
            out[it] = {"label": None, "how": "disagree"}
        elif len(given) == 1:
            out[it] = {"label": None, "how": "single"}
        else:
            out[it] = {"label": None, "how": "unlabelled"}
    return out


def _metrics(items: list[dict], final: dict[int, dict]) -> dict:
    """Precision of `coordinated`, FPR, and what humans say about the other verdicts, over
    items whose final human label is coordinated or organic. Weights undo the oversampling."""
    use = [(i, final[i["item"]]["label"]) for i in items if final[i["item"]]["label"] in DEFINITE]
    flagged = [(lab == "coordinated", i["weight"]) for i, lab in use
               if i["detector"]["status"] == "coordinated"]  # fmt: skip
    organic = [(i["detector"]["status"] == "coordinated", i["weight"]) for i, lab in use
               if lab == "organic"]  # fmt: skip
    chill = [(lab == "coordinated", i["weight"]) for i, lab in use
             if i["detector"]["status"] == "likely_organic"]  # fmt: skip
    abstain = [(lab == "coordinated", i["weight"]) for i, lab in use
               if i["detector"]["status"] == "insufficient"]  # fmt: skip
    cant = [i for i in items if final[i["item"]]["label"] == "cant_tell"]
    return {
        "n_definite": len(use),
        "n_cant_tell": len(cant),
        "precision": weighted_rate(flagged),
        "fpr": weighted_rate(organic),
        "coordinated_among_chill": weighted_rate(chill),
        "coordinated_among_cant_tell_verdicts": weighted_rate(abstain),
        "confusion": dict(Counter(f"{i['detector']['status']}->{lab}" for i, lab in use)),
    }


def score(sample: dict, labels: dict[str, dict[int, dict]], adj: dict[int, dict]) -> dict:
    items = sample["items"]
    ids = [i["item"] for i in items]
    final = final_labels(ids, labels, adj)
    pair = pick_pair(labels)
    agreement = None
    if pair:
        a, b = pair
        common = sorted(labels[a].keys() & labels[b].keys() & set(ids))
        three = [(labels[a][i]["label"], labels[b][i]["label"]) for i in common]
        two = [(x, y) for x, y in three if x in DEFINITE and y in DEFINITE]
        agreement = {
            "labellers": [a, b],
            "kappa_3way": cohen_kappa(three, LABELS),
            "kappa_definite": cohen_kappa(two, DEFINITE),
            "raw_agreement": weighted_rate([(x == y, 1.0) for x, y in three]),
        }
    by_split = {s: _metrics([i for i in items if i["split"] == s], final) for s in ("dev", "heldout")}
    return {
        "sample": sample["name"],
        "sample_rule": sample.get("rule_version"),
        "detector_versions": sample.get("detector_versions"),
        "n_items": len(items),
        "labellers": {name: len(v.keys() & set(ids)) for name, v in sorted(labels.items())},
        "resolution": dict(Counter(f["how"] for f in final.values())),
        "agreement": agreement,
        "all": _metrics(items, final),
        "by_split": by_split,
        "final": {str(k): v for k, v in final.items()},
    }


def format_report(r: dict) -> str:
    def rate(m: dict) -> str:
        if m["rate"] is None:
            return "n/a (n=0)"
        lo, hi = m["ci95"]
        return f"{m['rate']:.3f}  [{lo:.3f}, {hi:.3f}]  k={m['k']} n={m['n']} n_eff={m['n_eff']}"

    lines = [
        f"sample {r['sample']} ({r['n_items']} items, detector {r['detector_versions']})",
        f"labels per labeller: {r['labellers']}",
        f"resolution: {r['resolution']}",
    ]
    ag = r["agreement"]
    if ag:
        for key in ("kappa_3way", "kappa_definite"):
            k = ag[key]
            ci = f" [{k['ci95'][0]:.3f}, {k['ci95'][1]:.3f}]" if k["ci95"] else ""
            kv = "n/a" if k["kappa"] is None else f"{k['kappa']:.3f}"
            lines.append(f"{key} ({ag['labellers'][0]} vs {ag['labellers'][1]}): {kv}{ci} n={k['n']}")
    for name, m in [("all", r["all"]), *r["by_split"].items()]:
        lines += [
            f"-- {name}: {m['n_definite']} definite, {m['n_cant_tell']} can't tell",
            f"   precision(coordinated)       {rate(m['precision'])}",
            f"   false-positive rate          {rate(m['fpr'])}",
            f"   coordinated among Chill      {rate(m['coordinated_among_chill'])}",
            f"   coordinated among Can't tell {rate(m['coordinated_among_cant_tell_verdicts'])}",
        ]
    return "\n".join(lines)


def eval_rows(r: dict, sample: dict) -> list[dict]:
    """One eval_runs row per split, so the heldout number never mixes with dev."""
    rows = []
    for split, m in r["by_split"].items():
        if m["n_definite"] == 0:
            continue
        rows.append(
            {
                "dataset": DATASET,
                "split": split,
                "precision": m["precision"]["rate"],
                "fpr": m["fpr"]["rate"],
                "n": m["n_definite"],
                "details": {
                    "synthetic": False,
                    "what": "two humans label a frozen stratified sample of live clusters "
                    "(blind to detector status and score); precision of 'coordinated' and FPR "
                    "against the agreed/adjudicated label",
                    "sample": r["sample"],
                    "sample_rule": sample.get("rule"),
                    "sample_source": sample.get("source"),
                    "sample_created_at": sample.get("created_at"),
                    "detector_versions": r["detector_versions"],
                    "eval_commit": _git_sha(),
                    "split_rule": "window_start UTC hour: odd = heldout, even = dev",
                    "metrics": m,
                    "agreement": r["agreement"],
                    "resolution": r["resolution"],
                    "labellers": r["labellers"],
                    "population": sample.get("population"),
                    "strata": sample.get("strata"),
                    "items": [
                        {
                            "item": i["item"],
                            "cluster_id": i["detector"]["cluster_id"],
                            "status": i["detector"]["status"],
                            "score": i["detector"]["score"],
                            "weight": i["weight"],
                            "final": r["final"][str(i["item"])],
                        }
                        for i in sample["items"]
                        if i["split"] == split
                    ],
                    "ran_at": datetime.now(UTC).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
                },
            }
        )
    return rows

"""Hand-label eval (eval/labels.py, eval/label_server.py). Offline: no DB, no network."""

import json
import random

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from eval import labels as L
from eval.label_server import create_app

T0 = datetime(2026, 11, 13, 20, 0, tzinfo=UTC)  # even hour -> dev


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- kappa / rates


def test_kappa_perfect_and_chance():
    perfect = [("coordinated", "coordinated"), ("organic", "organic"), ("cant_tell", "cant_tell")]
    assert L.cohen_kappa(perfect)["kappa"] == 1.0
    # rater B always says organic: observed agreement equals chance agreement -> kappa 0
    pairs = [("coordinated", "organic"), ("organic", "organic")] * 5
    k = L.cohen_kappa(pairs, L.DEFINITE)
    assert k["kappa"] == 0.0
    assert k["n"] == 10


def test_kappa_textbook_value():
    # 2x2 table: both yes 20, A yes/B no 5, A no/B yes 10, both no 15 (n=50)
    # po = 0.7, pe = 0.5*0.6 + 0.5*0.4 = 0.5 -> kappa 0.4
    pairs = (
        [("coordinated", "coordinated")] * 20
        + [("coordinated", "organic")] * 5
        + [("organic", "coordinated")] * 10
        + [("organic", "organic")] * 15
    )
    k = L.cohen_kappa(pairs, L.DEFINITE)
    assert k["kappa"] == pytest.approx(0.4)
    assert k["observed"] == pytest.approx(0.7)
    assert k["expected"] == pytest.approx(0.5)
    lo, hi = k["ci95"]
    assert lo < 0.4 < hi


def test_kappa_undefined_and_empty():
    assert L.cohen_kappa([])["kappa"] is None
    same = [("organic", "organic")] * 4  # one category only: pe = 1
    assert L.cohen_kappa(same, L.DEFINITE)["kappa"] is None


def test_wilson_matches_known_interval():
    lo, hi = L.wilson(8, 10)
    assert (lo, hi) == (pytest.approx(0.4902, abs=1e-4), pytest.approx(0.9433, abs=1e-4))
    assert L.wilson(0, 0) is None
    lo, hi = L.wilson(0, 20)
    assert lo == 0.0 and 0 < hi < 0.2


def test_weighted_rate_equal_weights_is_plain_rate():
    r = L.weighted_rate([(True, 3.0)] * 8 + [(False, 3.0)] * 2)
    assert r["rate"] == 0.8 and r["n_eff"] == 10.0 and r["k"] == 8
    assert r["ci95"] == L.wilson(8, 10)


def test_weighted_rate_undoes_oversampling():
    # 1 hit from a stratum sampled 1-in-1, 1 miss from a stratum sampled 1-in-9
    r = L.weighted_rate([(True, 1.0), (False, 9.0)])
    assert r["rate"] == pytest.approx(0.1)
    assert r["n_eff"] < 2


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sampler


def _cands(n_co=10, n_org=200, n_ins=60, seed=1):
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out, cid = [], 0
    for status, k in (("coordinated", n_co), ("likely_organic", n_org), ("insufficient", n_ins)):
        for _ in range(k):
            cid += 1
            out.append(L.Candidate(cid, cid, status, round(rng.uniform(0.5, 1.0), 3), T0))
    return out


def test_sample_caps_rare_status_and_fills_total():
    picked, strata = L.stratified_sample(_cands(), 100, seed=7)
    assert len(picked) == 100
    by = {}
    for p in picked:
        by[p["candidate"].status] = by.get(p["candidate"].status, 0) + 1
    assert by["coordinated"] == 10  # only 10 exist: all of them
    assert by["likely_organic"] + by["insufficient"] == 90
    assert abs(by["likely_organic"] - by["insufficient"]) <= 1  # equal target shares
    assert sum(s["sampled"] for s in strata.values()) == 100
    assert len({p["candidate"].cluster_id for p in picked}) == 100  # no repeats


def test_sample_weights_and_bands():
    picked, strata = L.stratified_sample(_cands(), 100, seed=7)
    for p in picked:
        st = strata[p["stratum"]]
        assert p["weight"] == pytest.approx(st["population"] / st["sampled"])
        assert st["score_min"] <= p["candidate"].score <= st["score_max"]
    org = sorted((s for s in strata.values() if s["status"] == "likely_organic"),
                 key=lambda s: s["band"])  # fmt: skip
    assert len(org) == 4
    assert all(a["score_max"] <= b["score_min"] for a, b in zip(org, org[1:], strict=False))
    # weights sum to the population of each status
    tot = {}
    for p in picked:
        tot[p["candidate"].status] = tot.get(p["candidate"].status, 0) + p["weight"]
    assert tot["likely_organic"] == pytest.approx(200)
    assert tot["coordinated"] == pytest.approx(10)


def test_sample_is_deterministic_and_shuffled():
    a, _ = L.stratified_sample(_cands(), 50, seed=3)
    b, _ = L.stratified_sample(_cands(), 50, seed=3)
    assert [p["candidate"].cluster_id for p in a] == [p["candidate"].cluster_id for p in b]
    statuses = [p["candidate"].status for p in a]
    assert statuses != sorted(statuses)  # strata are interleaved in labelling order


def test_sample_smaller_population_than_n():
    picked, _ = L.stratified_sample(_cands(2, 3, 1), 100, seed=1)
    assert len(picked) == 6


def test_one_per_campaign():
    c = [L.Candidate(i, i // 3, "likely_organic", 0.6, T0) for i in range(9)]
    c += [L.Candidate(100, None, "coordinated", 0.9, T0), L.Candidate(101, None, "coordinated", 0.9, T0)]
    reps = L.one_per_campaign(c, random.Random(0))
    assert len(reps) == 3 + 2  # 3 campaigns, plus 2 clusters without a campaign
    assert len({r.campaign_id for r in reps if r.campaign_id is not None}) == 3


def test_split_rule():
    assert L.split_of(T0) == "dev"
    assert L.split_of(T0 + timedelta(hours=1)) == "heldout"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- evidence is blind


def _evidence():
    ws, we = T0, T0 + timedelta(minutes=10)
    members = [
        {"did": f"did:plc:m{i}", "role": "core", "handle": f"m{i}.bsky.social",

    posts = [

         "reply_to": None, "quote_uri": None, "embed_urls": ["https://xyz.example/"],
         "media_hashes": [], "text_hash": "h1"}
        for i in range(4)

    target = "at://did:plc:other/app.bsky.feed.post/t1"

    return L.build_evidence(ws, we, "10m", members, posts, actions,
                            {target: {"did": "did:plc:other", "text": "promo"}}, [])  # fmt: skip


def test_build_evidence_aggregates():
    e = _evidence()
    assert e["summary"]["accounts"] == 4
    assert e["summary"]["younger_than_30d"] == 4
    assert e["summary"]["reposts"] == 3

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reach the production Postgres (Hostinger VPS) from the team server, for eval reads/writes.
#   deploy/db-tunnel.sh start   # opens an SSH tunnel to a private unix socket, writes the env file
#   deploy/db-tunnel.sh stop
#   set -a; . ~/.config/noise-radar/prod-db.env; set +a   # then: --database-url "$PROD_DATABASE_URL"
# The DB port is never published on the VPS: the tunnel goes to the db container's address.
# The socket lives in a 0700 directory and the env file is 0600, so only you can use them.
# Env: HOSTINGER_HOST (required), HOSTINGER_USER (default root), HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY (optional),
#      HOSTINGER_DIR (default /opt/noise-radar). Nothing here prints the password.
set -euo pipefail

host=${HOSTINGER_HOST:?set HOSTINGER_HOST}
user=${HOSTINGER_USER:-root}
dir=${HOSTINGER_DIR:-/opt/noise-radar}
sock_dir=${PROD_DB_SOCK_DIR:-$HOME/.cache/noise-radar/prod-pg}
env_file=${PROD_DB_ENV:-$HOME/.config/noise-radar/prod-db.env}
ctl=$sock_dir/ssh.ctl
ssh_opts=(-o BatchMode=yes -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes)
if [[ -n ${HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY:-} ]]; then ssh_opts+=(-i "$HOSTINGER_SSH_KEY" -o IdentitiesOnly=yes); fi

case ${1:-} in
  start)
    install -d -m 700 "$sock_dir" "$(dirname "$env_file")"
    if ssh -S "$ctl" -O check "$user@$host" 2>/dev/null; then echo "tunnel already up"; exit 0; fi
    ip=$(ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$user@$host" \
      "docker inspect -f '{{range .NetworkSettings.Networks}}{{.IPAddress}}{{end}}' noise-radar-db-1")
    creds=$(ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" "$user@$host" "grep -E '^POSTGRES_(USER|PASSWORD|DB)=' '$dir/.env'")
    pg_user=$(sed -n 's/^POSTGRES_USER=//p' <<<"$creds")
    pg_pass=$(sed -n 's/^POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED <<<"$creds")
    pg_db=$(sed -n 's/^POSTGRES_DB=//p' <<<"$creds")
    rm -f "$sock_dir/.s.PGSQL.5432"
    ssh "${ssh_opts[@]}" -f -N -M -S "$ctl" -o StreamLocalBindUnlink=yes -o StreamLocalBindMask=0177 \
      -L "$sock_dir/.s.PGSQL.5432:$ip:5432" "$user@$host"
    pass_enc=$(python3 -c 'import sys, urllib.parse; print(urllib.parse.quote(sys.argv[1], safe=""))' "$pg_pass")
    (umask 177; printf 'PROD_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://%s:%s@/%s?host=%s&port=5432\n' \
      "$pg_user" "$pass_enc" "$pg_db" "$sock_dir" >"$env_file")
    echo "tunnel up: socket $sock_dir/.s.PGSQL.5432, env in $env_file (PROD_DATABASE_URL)"
    ;;
  stop)
    ssh -S "$ctl" -O exit "$user@$host" 2>/dev/null && echo "tunnel closed" || echo "no tunnel"
    ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: $0 start|stop" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

**How to label.** Open the page (through an SSH tunnel: `ssh -L 8001:127.0.0.1:8001 <team server>`,
then http://127.0.0.1:8001/), type your name once, and judge each item on its own: a group of
accounts and everything they did in one time window (timeline, posts several of them engaged
with, repeated texts, links, follows, account ages, followers, avatars, their posts, with
bsky.app links). Press **1** coordinated (acting together; hard to explain as independent
people), **2** organic (plausibly independent: news, viral posts, fandoms, conversation) or **3**
can't tell; it saves and moves on. **n** adds a note, arrows move. You never see the detector's
status, score, signals or analyst verdict, and you shouldn't look the group up on the dashboard.
Two people label every item separately; when both are done, the *disagreements* view shows both
labels and you record one adjudicated label together.

**How the number is made.** `sample` reads clusters from the live database that haven't been
updated for 15 minutes (synthetic excluded), keeps one random episode per campaign (episodes of
one campaign are near copies), and draws a stratified sample: detector status (40% coordinated,
30% likely_organic, 30% insufficient as targets, capped at what exists) x 4 equal-count score
bands. It freezes each cluster's evidence at that moment into
`/srv/junction-espoo/data/labels/samples/<name>.json` (outside git: it's real Bluesky content;
write-once). Labels go to `<name>.labels.jsonl` next to it, append-only, latest per person and item
wins. `score` takes a final label per item (both agree, or the adjudicated label; disagreements
and single labels don't count until resolved; "can't tell" is reported but left out of the
rates), then computes:
- **Agreement**: Cohen's kappa between the two labellers on all three answers and on items both
  answered definitely, with an approximate 95% CI, plus raw agreement.
- **Precision** = share of detector-`coordinated` items that humans call coordinated.
- **FPR** = share of human-organic items the detector flagged `coordinated`. Statuses are sampled
  at different rates, so every item carries weight = stratum population / stratum sample size;
  rates are weighted and their 95% Wilson interval uses the Kish effective n. With equal weights
  this is plain k/n.
- Also reported: share of `likely_organic` (Chill) and `insufficient` items that humans call
  coordinated, and the full status->label confusion.

Each split (window start hour, odd = `heldout`, even = `dev`, same rule as above) gets its own
`eval_runs` row. Error analysis may read `dev` items only.

Limits: the population is clusters the live worker stored, not all of Bluesky, so FPR is "of the
groups we surfaced that humans call organic, how many we flagged", not a rate over all organic
activity, and missed campaigns that never formed a cluster aren't measured here. Coordinated
clusters are rare, so the precision interval is wide; it says so in `n` and `ci95`. Humans can be
wrong too: kappa is how much to trust the labels.

'''
